title: Predicted Composite Signed-Distance Fields for Real-Time Motion Planning in Dynamic Environments
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of real-time motion planning for robots operating in dynamic environments with moving obstacles. The authors argue that conventional signed-distance field (SDF) approaches are too slow to recompute online, and that planners which ignore obstacle motion or use only binary collision costs can produce inefficient or unsafe trajectories.

To solve this, the paper introduces predicted signed-distance fields and a composite SDF method that updates the environment representation by combining precomputed SDFs for static and moving objects. The approach uses a constant-velocity model to predict obstacle motion and integrates the resulting predicted SDFs with the GPMP2 motion planner, allowing obstacle factors in the factor graph to be updated in real time.

The work is evaluated in simulation and hardware with 7-DoF robotic arms, including a WAM arm and a Franka Emika Panda, navigating around moving obstacles such as a pillar or a mobile robot. Results show that composite SDF prediction is substantially faster than exact recomputation, and that including predicted obstacle trajectories improves the likelihood of collision-free planning and reduces trajectory jerk, producing smoother behavior than execute-and-update baselines.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a robotics motion-planning paper, not an education study, and it does not evaluate any K-12 instructional intervention. There is no relevant educational methodology or learner/teacher outcome evidence to rate under the requested framework.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports technical performance improvements in robot motion planning, not educational impact. No K-12 teaching, learning, coaching, or teacher-planning outcomes are studied.
